description: Acceptance registered before vendored MTS-ESP shim evaluation. No physical CS-80 law is inferred by this modern software-protocol adapter.

mts_client.fixture: A deterministic fake of the upstream C API returns twelve-tone notes shifted by one quarter semitone and marks note 60 unmapped; the real shim must query all 128 notes with channel -1, produce the corresponding pitch/mapping table, forward nonempty MIDI buffers, preserve the table when no master is present, and balance registration/deregistration.
mts_client.native_fixture: Compile and run the actual unmodified upstream client plus the shipping shim in a standalone test process; available must be true, no master must leave the supplied table unchanged, repeated instance lifetime must complete, and the upstream client must parse a standard one-note MTS SysEx retuning without a master.
mts_client.policy_invariance: Engine renders supplied with the shim-produced tuning table must be byte-identical to the same untuned renders both at the default tuning mode 0 and in PURE CS-80 with tuning mode 2. A modern tuning-mode-2 render must differ, proving the fixture exercises tuning.
mts_client.mutations: Unavailable stub in shipping branch; dropped mapped-key flag; dropped registration/deregistration; wrong pitch conversion; disabled Pure/default tuning policy guard. Every implemented acceptance gate receives a deliberately broken negative control.
